title: Core: Viewport UX fixes
body:
## What I did

- Ensure values on drag handles respect minimum viewport size
- Update values on drag handles to account for zoom scale factor
- Fix scrollIntoView when dragging
- Prevent panel drag handle from rendering outside of container
- Prevent floating point numbers on drag handles

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Resizing enforces minimum dimensions, aborts invalid drags early, and applies correct final size when dragging ends.

* **Improvements**
  * Edge-drag behavior and auto-scrolling are more reliable with edge tracking; drag handles show scaled, rounded dimensions and react to canvas scale changes.
  * Overlapping resizer behavior refined for panel placements.

* **Refactor**
  * Layout sizing centralized via CSS-variable driven styles, simplifying component props.

comments.author: coderabbitai
comments.label_reasoning: The comment identifies incorrect clamping logic where minimum viewport values are applied after scaling instead of before, causing drift from the true minimum and contradicting requirements.

review_threads.actionability_reasoning: Identifies a bug with scaling/clamping logic and provides a concrete suggested fix.

comments.author: ndelangen
comments.body:
I'd prefer if we would use more descriptive names.

I do not know what the `n`, `u`, `v` prefixes stand for.
comments.label_reasoning: The comment explicitly calls out unclear variable name prefixes (n, u, v) and requests more descriptive names.

review_threads.actionability_reasoning: Requests renaming variables to be more descriptive — a concrete style/naming change.

comments.author: ndelangen
comments.body:
```suggestion
    // we use css-custom-properties here, to prevent Emotion from generating a new CSS-className on every resize
    gridTemplateColumns: `minmax(0, var(--nav-width)) minmax(${MINIMUM_CONTENT_WIDTH_PX}px, 1fr) minmax(0, var(--right-panel-width))`,
    gridTemplateRows: `1fr minmax(0, var(--bottom-panel-height))`,
```
comments.label_reasoning: The suggestion adds a comment explaining the use of CSS custom properties to prevent Emotion from generating new class names on every resize, clarifying the intent of the code.

review_threads.actionability_reasoning: Provides a direct code suggestion to change the CSS template strings.
